recent_posts.title: Why You Must Check Your Password Manager Immediately | THREAT WIRE
Vercel Hacked: A Simple Failure of OAuth Hygiene | THREAT WIRE
recent_posts.summary: A weekly cybersecurity news roundup covering several major stories. The main story involves a Vercel data breach traced back to a compromised OAuth token from a Context.ai security incident, where an employee had granted excessive Google Workspace permissions to a third-party app. The host argues this was fundamentally an OAuth hygiene failure and shadow IT problem, not an AI-driven attack as Vercel's CEO framed it. Other stories include: Claude Opus (referred to as 'Mythos') achieving 73% success on expert-level CTF tasks and completing a 32-step corporate network attack simulation; NIST announcing it will deprioritize CVE enrichment in the NVD due to a 263% surge in submissions since 2020; Cal.com moving from open source to closed source citing AI security concerns; and brief mentions of Zoom's AI detection feature, Trail of Bits beating Google's ZK proof, and Meta partnering with PortSwigger for Burp Suite licenses.

recent_posts.title: Use after free vulnerabilities found in Chrome and Firefox
recent_posts.summary: Critical use-after-free vulnerabilities were discovered in both Chrome and Firefox. Chrome/Chromium was affected by CVE-2026-5281, a zero-day in Dawn (the open-source WebGPU implementation) that could allow arbitrary code execution via a crafted HTML page. Firefox was hit by CVE-2022-64688, a CVSS 10.0 sandbox escape through a use-after-free bug in the accessibility API, affecting Firefox and related browsers. The host notes a perceived increase in use-after-free vulnerabilities in the wild and invites engineers to share what languages are susceptible and what to look for in code reviews.

recent_posts.title: Axios npm package compromised in software supply chain attack
recent_posts.summary: Team PCP, a threat actor group, has been escalating software supply chain attacks, compromising GitHub Actions, DockerHub, npm, and other platforms. Cisco suffered a data breach with stolen AWS keys used for unauthorized activities. Most critically, two versions of the widely-used Axios npm package (with 100M+ and 37M weekly downloads) were compromised on March 31st, 2026, by a suspected North Korean attacker group. The malicious versions contained a package deploying a multi-stage payload capable of arbitrary command execution and data exfiltration. Attackers hijacked the lead maintainer's account to suppress warnings. Google researchers warn these attacks will continue, with hundreds of thousands of stolen secrets potentially enabling further supply chain attacks, ransomware, SaaS compromises, and cryptocurrency theft. The author recommends rotating all secrets associated with public npm packages as a precaution.

recent_posts.title: Age verification laws for internet and social media spread across multiple countries
recent_posts.summary: California passed a law requiring operating systems to collect age information from users, set to take effect in 2027, though concerns already exist around multi-use computers and implementation clarity. Apple has begun rolling out age verification in the UK with iOS 26.4, requiring driver's licenses, IDs, or credit cards — leaving many without valid documents unable to verify. France's Senate voted to support a two-tier social media system based on age verification, and Greece is moving toward a social media ban for minors. The host expresses strong personal support for age-restricting social media, comparing today's inaction to historical failures to protect public health.

recent_posts.title: Chrome Terminates Cookie Stealing Malware - Threat Wire
recent_posts.summary: A weekly cybersecurity news roundup covering several major stories: Chrome 136 introduces Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC), hardware-based protections that cryptographically link session cookies to a device's TPM or Secure Enclave to prevent cookie theft. Anthropic's Project Glasswing and the Claude Mythos model are discussed in depth — the model autonomously found and exploited vulnerabilities at a dramatically higher rate than previous Claude versions, achieving full control flow hijack on 10 patched targets, though Anthropic says these capabilities emerged unintentionally and the model won't be publicly released. Other stories include California's OS-level age verification law, Apple's age checks in iOS for UK users, France and Greece moving toward social media age restrictions, GitHub Copilot briefly inserting ads into pull requests, an Adobe Reader zero-day exploited since December 2025, the FBI retrieving deleted Signal messages via iOS notifications, and France planning a government-wide migration from Windows to Linux.

recent_posts.title: Team PCP supply chain attacks, FCC router ban, and Delve compliance fraud
recent_posts.summary: A cybersecurity weekly roundup covering several major stories. Team PCP, a threat actor falsely claiming Israeli origins, carried out a rapid series of software supply chain attacks in March 2026, compromising tools like Trivy, a static IaC analysis tool, and LiteLLM by injecting credential-stealing malware via compromised GitHub Actions credentials. The attacks spanned GitHub Actions, DockerHub, npm, and PyPI. The FCC announced a ban on foreign-made consumer routers citing national security risks, though the approved alternatives list currently only includes drones. Compliance startup Delve was exposed for generating fraudulent audit reports using certification mills rather than real CPA firms, with an ongoing multi-part exposé. Additionally, Cloudflare was found injecting tracking scripts into hosted pages via its Web Analytics real user measurement feature.

recent_posts.title: Two iOS exploit kits and Android sideloading changes in this week's security news
recent_posts.summary: A cybersecurity news roundup covering two iOS exploit kits (Karuna and Dark Sword) discovered in early 2026, both likely deployed by the same threat actor. Karuna targeted iOS 13.0–17.2.1 using 23 exploits across five chains, while Dark Sword targets iOS 18.4–18.7 with near-zero interaction required, leveraging WebGPU and kernel read/write access. Apple has issued patches and recommends updating or enabling Lockdown Mode. Also covered: Google/Android rolling back strict sideloading restrictions in favor of a new 'advanced flow' verification process with a 24-hour delay to deter scam-pressured installs, Nvidia's NemoClaw secure OpenClaw stack, a breathalyzer company hack, and a Super Micro co-founder arrest for GPU smuggling.
